adoption.notes: The runtime verifies each firmware fault under its own v: v 1 under v1's closed sets, v 2 under this version's, any other v refused, and drives this version's corpus through its ingest gate. Its module docstring and capability matrix describe the v 2 sets as this draft's and make no conformance claim, so the version is not frozen by this merge. It verifies signatures with OpenSSL behind its ed25519-key-admission/v1 admission. That combination reaches every verdict of the ed25519-verification/v1 corpus when the corpus is run on the host, OpenSSL alone differing only on the keys admission refuses, but the runtime does not yet drive that corpus through its ingest gate. From 1ddc3e9 it also enforces Device Mode at registration, at promotion of a pending candidate, and on every message against a stored anchor, and drives this version's manifest corpus through its registration path: every accepted case registers and every refusal is refused for its reason and stores nothing. It reads no authority or trust grade from the mode. From 72eb2b4 it implements Controller Profiles: registration applies the four refusals and the one-profile rule, profile documents are held by digest only when canonical and valid, a bridged measurement outside its document's range is refused, and health shows each alarm channel as unknown or as of the reading it came from, with the silence bound on a clock that counts suspend; it vendored this version's profile corpus at f3e980d, and now pins every corpus of this version at 4880b99. That is implementation, not end-to-end or HIL proof. From a39d551b it accepts the reading envelope at v 2 and its liveness_nonce, and computes the reading-age bound in memory, on a clock that counts suspend; the bound is computed only while liveness v 2 publication is on, which it is not by default. From 02b33b1d its manifest parser reads runtime_key_domains and refuses any other value as invalid_runtime_key_domains, and it signs no command and no liveness message for a device that does not declare it; the v2.5.0 release accepts and ignores the key. Neither is released.

The device signs every fault at v 2 and has no path to v 1; faults it buffered before adopting are retransmitted at v 1 as stored. It mirrors this version's fault corpus byte for byte, copied from ori-specs 3159506 and pinned by digest in its golden-vector README; it carries no vector manifest, so no vendored revision is recorded. Its DECISIONS.md says core/fault_event.c implements the fault object this version defines; that sentence was written while the firmware was built alongside this draft, and the maintainer ruled on 2026-10-09 that it is provenance, not a conformance claim, so the version is not frozen by this merge and stays amendable. From 9932044 it signs a controller_profile on each bridged channel; its controller library is locked empty, so its build ships no controller profile. From a2c528f every manifest it signs declares runtime_key_domains, and from ee35e34 it accepts liveness at v 2 and holds its nonce under firmware-commands/v2. It signs every envelope at v 1 and signs no liveness_nonce.

notes: Exists so a device can sign a command_rejected fault whose detail is rate_limited: the fault object carries v 2, under which the closed detail sets are the ones this version lists. Manifest and maintenance events keep v 1; the manifest gains Device Mode validation and, on bridged channels, a controller_profile naming the digest of the profile that decoded it. The reading envelope may carry v 2 with liveness_nonce, the nonce of the runtime liveness message the device held when the measurement began, from which only the runtime that signed that message can bound, from above, how long ago the device began the transaction behind the reading; the bound dates that transaction, not the measured quantity. The runtime accepts envelope v 2 and computes the reading-age bound on its main branch; no producer signs envelope v 2 yet. The manifest may declare runtime_key_domains: the device verifies in the signing domains of firmware-commands/v2 and accepts runtime liveness at v 2, and a runtime publishes liveness to it at v 2 alone. The edge firmware declares it and the runtime reads it, both on their main branches only. The runtime verifies v 2 faults and the edge firmware signs them; the evidence authority and sdk-python have not adopted it. Every verifier, the runtime first, adopts it before the devices whose faults it reads: a v1-only verifier refuses every v 2 fault. Envelope v 2 is adopted consumers first: verifiers accept it, devices accept liveness v 2, the runtime publishes it, and devices sign envelope v 2 last.
